gappers.catalyst_detail: This is a gap-up-and-fail, not a gap-down. CRWV rose ~4% premarket on NVDA's Q3 beat and raised FY guidance (Benzinga, ~09:00 ET), opened at $51.07, then sold off to a $46.33 session low; the 10:09 ET scan snapshot caught $47.2476, -5.30% vs the $49.89 prior close. Benzinga's live tape read $48.08 / -3.64% at 10:10 ET and an independent Alpaca re-check at 10:16 ET read $47.93 / -3.93%, so the -5.30% scan print was near the low and the name has since recovered part of it. No CRWV-specific negative headline exists for the reversal. Standing context: Q3 EPS -$0.95 vs -$1.53 est (Nov 10), then six analyst PT cuts in four days (DA Davidson $100->$45, Barclays $105->$85, Argus $150->$100, Evercore $150->$100, Truist $165->$115, Macquarie $130->$120) against one raise (Citi $128->$149); -32% in October on neocloud debt concerns; RSI 39; short interest 23.82% with 1.07 days to cover; 52-week range $40.58-$138.25; market cap $26.2B.
gappers.why: Sector-wide relief rally failing, not a company event. NVDA's beat bid up the whole neocloud complex premarket; as NVDA gave back its entire +3.6% premarket gain and turned red (-0.70%, $154.38 at 10:16 ET vs $161.09 premarket), the highest-beta derivatives of that trade were sold hardest. CRWV -- the most debt-levered neocloud, 23.8% short -- travelled furthest. Mechanically a failed-breakout/gap-fill, with the overhang of last week's PT-cut wave capping any bid.
gappers.impact: Reads as a one-day headline spike that already mean-reverted, inside about 40 minutes of the open -- not sustainable. Volume is the tell against durability: 15.6M vs a 45.5M 30-day average, so neither the pop nor the flush is volume-confirmed. Sector read-through is unambiguous and confirms the move is not idiosyncratic: NBIS, which this routine logged at +10.27% premarket at 09:09 ET, is now +0.10% ($106.14) with the entire gap erased; IREN -1.70%; NVDA itself -0.70%; QQQ only +0.34%. The whole AI-compute complex round-tripped its NVDA-beat gap within the first 45 minutes.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: A failed relief bounce inside an established downtrend -- no structural catalyst, six PT cuts in the past week, RSI 39, and the $40.58 52-week low only ~13% below spot; nothing here justifies carrying past the session.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Account is flat ($100,000 equity, 0/6 positions, 0% deployed vs the 75-85% rule, 0/3 weekly trade slots used), so no existing holding would be displaced and nothing else on today's list competes -- CRWV is the sole qualifier and OPEN was excluded at $1.28. The real cost is sequencing: spending one of three weekly slots going long a name that just failed at the open while its own sector leader (NVDA) went red. R:R is marginal at best. The 3%-minimum stop rule caps a stop at $46.49 or lower, and respecting the $46.33 session low pushes it to ~$46.00 (~4.0% risk), which needs a ~$51.79 target (+8.1%) to clear 2:1 -- above today's $51.07 open and day high, so the trade only pays 2:1 if the failed gap is fully reclaimed. Research only: no size proposed, no order placed.
